words.gloss: the two-fold state (of birth and liberation)

literal: The two-fold state's nature having understood, here virtue those who embraced, [their] greatness shone in the world.
translation: The greatness of those who have understood the nature of both states of existence and have embraced virtue here in this world, shines supreme over the world.
modern: பிறப்பு, வீடுபேறு ஆகிய இரண்டின் தன்மையையும் ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து, இவ்வுலகில் அறநெறியை மேற்கொண்டவர்களின் பெருமையே உலகத்தில் உயர்ந்ததாக விளங்குகின்றது.
explanation: This couplet praises the greatness of those who have renounced worldly desires. The word 'irumai' refers to the two-fold state of existence, representing the transient life of birth and the eternal state of liberation. By deeply analyzing and understanding the nature of these two states, wise sages choose to practice supreme virtue ('aṟam') while living in this world ('īṇṭu'). The poet emphasizes that the greatness of such individuals who have mastered this understanding shines as the most exalted thing in the world.
